DIOPTRA / HERO OF ALEXANDRIA, CHAPTER 15

Meet beneath
the mountain.

Fixed portals, a chosen circuit, and two outside aiming triangles.

Reopen these settings. This file embeds its diagrams, fonts, eight readings and four source pages. Opening it makes no external requests.

The signed field book

These are chosen modern metre lengths, not measurements from an ancient tunnel. The source's five-to-one ratio is an example; the two- and seven-to-one settings are modern exercises.

Each measured leg, with its signed displacement

Rightward 400 − leftward 100 = 300 m. Perpendicular net displacement: 60 m. These are plan directions, not elevation changes. The ideal hidden line has length 305.9412 m.

Save the full coordinate and measurement CSV

The aiming triangle

ΒΝ : ΔΝ = 300 : 60 = 5 : 1. With an outside baseline of 50 m, the ideal perpendicular is 10 m. Your chosen perpendicular is 10 m.

The chosen error is 10 mm at both entrances. Positive error moves a peg farther from its own baseline. At the middle cross-section, the Β line is at y = 30.03 m and the Δ line at y = 29.97 m; their vertical gap is 60 mm.

The original proof assumes exact alignments. The peg displacement is a modern deterministic experiment, not an estimate of ancient accuracy. It changes only the aiming pegs, leaving the traverse exact. The separate gap detail has its own scale.

Read the Greek

Selected excerpts from Schöne's 1903 edition, adapted from the Harvard College Library / Open Greek and Latin digital transcription. New English translation and grammar. Line-end hyphens and whitespace are joined, standard Δ replaces ∠, apostrophes are normalized, and line numbers and apparatus are omitted here. Angle brackets preserve editorial supplements. Greek selections and new teaching text: CC BY-SA 4.0.

Dioptra 15 · p. 238, lines 2–4

1. The entrances are given

Ὄρος διορύξαι ἐπ’ εὐθείας τῶν στομάτων τοῦ ὀρύγματος ἐν τῷ ὄρει δοθέντων.

To bore through a mountain in a straight line, when the mouths of the excavation in the mountain have been given.

τῶν στομάτων … δοθέντων · the mouths having been given

A genitive absolute: a genitive noun and participle set the condition. Στόμα means ‘mouth’; here it names a tunnel entrance. Διορύξαι is an aorist active infinitive stating the task, not a report that the work happened in the past.

Both portals are fixed before the outside circuit is chosen. Moving the bends does not move the entrances.

Dioptra 15 · p. 238, lines 6–8

2. Begin with a line you can choose

ἤγαγον εὐθεῖαν ἀπὸ τοῦ Β ἐν τῷ ἐδάφει τὴν ΒΕ, ὡς ἔτυχεν· καὶ ἀπὸ τυχόντος τοῦ Ε τῇ ΒΕ πρὸς ὀρθὰς ἤγαγον τὴν ΕΖ διὰ τῆς διόπτρας·

I drew a straight line ΒΕ from Β on the ground, as it happened; and from a point Ε chosen at will I drew ΕΖ at right angles to ΒΕ by means of the dioptra.

πρὸς ὀρθὰς · at right angles

The feminine plural ὀρθὰς leaves ‘angles’ understood. Διὰ with the genitive τῆς διόπτρας names the means: ‘by means of the dioptra’. A line chosen at will need not point toward the hidden entrance.

Follow ΒΕ, then turn a right angle onto ΕΖ. Change the circuit and watch the net displacement stay fixed.

Dioptra 15 · p. 240, lines 1–3

3. Close the circuit with a perpendicular sight

ἂν διὰ τῆς πρὸς ὀρθὰς θέσεως τοῦ κανόνος φανῇ τὸ Δ σημεῖον. πεφηνέτω ⟨οὔσης τῆς διόπτρας κατὰ τὸ Μ⟩· ἔσται δὴ ἡ ΜΔ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ΚΛ κάθετος.

…until point Δ comes into view through setting the sighting rule at right angles. Let it have appeared with the dioptra at Μ; then ΜΔ will be perpendicular to ΚΛ.

κάθετος · perpendicular

The adjective describes ΜΔ relative to the line ΚΛ. The opening ἂν continues ‘until’ from the preceding page. Angle brackets retain Schöne’s supplied words; the instrument’s position at Μ is editorially explicit here.

The measured circuit ends Κ–Μ–Δ. Λ belongs to the longer sight line. It is not an extra measured corner in this model.

Dioptra 15 · p. 240, lines 3–5

4. Imagine the triangle you cannot measure directly

καὶ νενοήσθω ἐκβεβλημένη ἡ ΕΒ ἐπὶ τὸ Ν, καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτὴν κάθετος ἡ ΔΝ.

And let ΕΒ be imagined extended to Ν, with ΔΝ perpendicular to it.

νενοήσθω · let it be imagined

A perfect passive imperative asks the reader to hold a construction in mind. The line inside the mountain is not another accessible measuring path. Ν is the foot of the perpendicular from Δ to the extended baseline.

Subtract leftward distances from rightward ones to obtain ΒΝ. Sum the perpendicular signed distances to obtain ΔΝ.

Dioptra 15 · p. 240, lines 9–10

5. Five times is an example, not a universal rule

εὑρήσθω οὖν, εἰ τύχοι, πενταπλῆ ἡ ΒΝ τῆς ΔΝ

Suppose, then, for example, that ΒΝ has been found to be five times ΔΝ.

πενταπλῆ · fivefold; five times as large

The feminine adjective agrees with the understood straight line ΒΝ. The genitive τῆς ΔΝ supplies the comparison. Εἰ τύχοι makes this an example; it does not prescribe a five-to-one ratio for every tunnel.

The default circuit gives 300:60 = 5:1. Only that ratio comes from the example; the metre lengths are chosen. Try a different exercise to see the construction generalize.

Dioptra 15 · p. 240, lines 15–17

6. Make a small similar triangle outside

λαβόντες οὖν ἐπὶ τῆς ΒΕ σημεῖον τυχὸν τὸ Ο, καὶ πρὸς ὀρθὰς ἀγαγόντες τὴν ΟΞ τῇ ΒΟ, πέμπτον μέρος θήσομεν τὴν ΟΞ τῆς ΒΟ.

Taking, then, any point Ο on the line ΒΕ, and drawing ΟΞ at right angles to ΒΟ, we shall make ΟΞ one fifth of ΒΟ.

πέμπτον μέρος · a fifth part

The fractional expression reverses the comparison: if the long leg is five times the short one, the short leg is one fifth of the long one. The figure places Ο on the extension beyond Β. ‘Line ΒΕ’ need not mean only the finite segment between the two letters.

Set the outside baseline, then place the perpendicular peg. In the five-to-one example, a 50 m baseline needs a 10 m perpendicular.

Dioptra 15 · p. 240, lines 20–22

7. Extend both outside lines inward

διορύξομεν οὖν ἀπὸ μὲν τοῦ Β ποιοῦντες τὸ ὄρυγμα ἐπ’ εὐθείας τῆς ΒΞ, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ Δ ἐπ’ εὐθείας τῆς ΔΠ.

We shall therefore bore through, making the excavation from Β in a straight line with ΒΞ, and from Δ in a straight line with ΔΠ.

ἀπὸ μὲν … ἀπὸ δὲ · from the one … from the other

The paired particles coordinate the two starting points. Ἀπό takes the genitive. The construction uses exterior sights to establish an inward direction; no sight line through the intact mountain is assumed.

Extend Ξ–Β and Π–Δ into the mountain. The small triangles give collinear lines when their proportions agree with the hidden triangle.

Dioptra 15 · p. 240, lines 24–26

8. The workers will meet

γινομένου τοῦ ὀρύγματος οὕτως ὑπαντήσουσιν ἀλλήλοις οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι.

With the excavation made in this way, the workers will meet one another.

ὑπαντήσουσιν ἀλλήλοις · they will meet one another

Ὑπαντήσουσιν is future active, third-person plural; οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι, ‘the workers’, is its subject. The reciprocal pronoun ἀλλήλοις is dative. The mathematical conclusion depends on the stated alignments being maintained.

Reveal the middle cross-section. Then deliberately displace an outside peg: the ideal proof and a perturbed physical setting are different experiments.

Source decisions and limits

A planar reading of Hero’s construction. The metres, route coordinates and mountain outline are chosen. This is not a reconstruction of Samos, an elevation survey or an estimate of ancient instrument accuracy. No claim is made that Eupalinos used this later-described method at Samos.

The printed construction establishes Μ as the closing perpendicular sight station on ΚΛ. Subsequent printed summation lists use ΚΛ and ΛΔ. The model sums the measured ΚΜ and ΜΔ, retaining the full printed pages so that the reading decision is inspectable. The figure places Ο outside Β, on the extended line ΒΕ; the model follows that exterior placement.

The mountain is a synthetic outline. Contour-like lines are decorative, not measured elevations. The extension control describes a fraction of each half's horizontal span, not elapsed time or equal drilling distances. The middle gap is vertical at that station, not the shortest separation of two infinite lines.
